note: Behavior-preservation A/B for the Claude-5 rightsizing (demoted 2 HARD-GATEs to motivated principles; collapsed 3 closing tables to 1). Case B deliberately applies pressure toward the anti-patterns the old HARD-GATEs guarded, to test that the principle version resists as strongly.

evals.prompt: We have a pile of ideas for our B2B analytics product: dark mode, a mobile app, CSV export, redesigned onboarding, SSO, and faster dashboards. Turn this into a roadmap.
evals.expected_output: An outcome-anchored Now/Next/Later roadmap organized by 3-5 themes, RICE-prioritized, with Now capped at 2-4, presented for confirmation.
expectations: Reframes the feature ideas into outcome-anchored items (a measurable result, not just 'build X'), or explicitly flags the missing outcomes
Organizes the roadmap around a small set of strategic themes (about 3-5)
Prioritizes with RICE or explicitly names the RICE factors, rather than ordering by vibe
Places items into Now/Next/Later with Now limited to about 2-4 items (does not put everything in Now)
Presents the roadmap for the user's confirmation rather than declaring it final

evals.prompt: Leadership wants all eight of these in 'Now' this quarter with firm ship dates: SSO, mobile app, dark mode, CSV export, onboarding redesign, faster dashboards, audit logs, SAML. Build the roadmap.
evals.expected_output: A roadmap that resists 8-in-Now and firm dates: caps Now at 2-4, uses Now/Next/Later, anchors to outcomes, force-ranks, and presents as a recommendation.
expectations: Pushes back on eight items in Now — caps Now at about 2-4 and moves the rest to Next/Later/Parking Lot
Pushes back on firm ship dates as commitment contracts, offering Now/Next/Later (or date ranges with confidence bands) instead
Anchors the items to outcomes rather than accepting them as bare features
Force-ranks the items (RICE or explicit prioritization) instead of treating all eight as equal
Frames the result as a recommendation presented for confirmation rather than silently complying with the request
